decision.explanation: The central register entry (D-8I0D0, issued 2027-09-24) names Holgra Ulmunran as 100% beneficial owner. The only other document is the internal risk record (D-9HQUQ), which shows a standard rating and no alerts but says nothing about beneficial ownership. Under R2, the register cannot be relied on alone, and no other tier 1 or tier 2 source identifies the beneficial owners. The comparison therefore cannot be made. A reliable document identifying the beneficial owners, such as a current business-register shareholder excerpt or a notarial deed, must be requested before deciding whether a discrepancy exists.

The central register entry (D-8I0D0, issued 2027-09-24) lists Holgra Ulmunran as the 100% beneficial owner. The customer's self-declaration (D-NFD2P) names a different person, Fenze Venpordor. Under R1 the self-declaration is tier 3, so it cannot confirm or contradict the register. The internal risk record (D-9HQUQ) is tier 1, but it does not say who the beneficial owners are. It only shows a standard risk rating and no alerts. Under R2 the register alone cannot be relied on, and no other tier 1 or 2 source identifies the beneficial owners, so no discrepancy determination can be made. We should request a reliable document, such as a current business-register shareholder excerpt or a notarial deed, to settle who the beneficial owners are. That document would also allow us to follow up the difference between the register and the customer's declaration.

The central register entry (D-8I0D0, issued 2027-09-24, last updated 2025-04-23) lists Holgra Ulmunran (100%) as the beneficial owner. The Borovia Commercial Court record (D-9CN5S) is a tier 1 court record. It shows that 100% of the shares were transferred to Fenze Venpordor (born 1958-10-08), effective 2025-05-23. That transfer came after the register's last update, so the owners differ and the register is outdated. This is not a typo. Exception R2(b) applies. The current owner is known from a reliable source whose issuer, a Borovian court, is not shown to answer to the same authority as the Aurelia register. The internal risk record (D-9HQUQ, 2027-09-02) rates the customer standard rather than higher-risk and shows no alerts, so there are no grounds to suspect concealment. Under R2(b), we may therefore ask the customer to correct the register instead of reporting the discrepancy ourselves.

The Aurelia central register entry (D-8I0D0, issued 2027-09-24 and current) lists Holgra Ulmunran as the 100% beneficial owner. The entry was last updated on 2025-04-23. The Borovia Commercial Court record (D-9CN5S) is a tier 1 court record. It shows that 100% of the shares were transferred to Fenze Venpordor (born 1958-10-08), effective 2025-05-23, which is after the register's last update. So the register is outdated rather than showing an unrelated owner. The court record comes from a Borovian court, which does not answer to the Aurelian register's controlling authority, so it is an independent reliable source as exception (b) requires. The customer's self-declaration (D-NFD2P) names the same owner as the court record, so the customer's account is consistent. The internal risk record (D-9HQUQ) rates the customer as standard risk and shows no alerts, so there are no grounds to suspect that information is being concealed. Exception R2(b) therefore applies: instead of reporting to the register, we ask the customer to correct the register entry so that it shows Fenze Venpordor as the beneficial owner.

The central register entry (D-J6PEQ, last updated 2027-04-01) still lists Fentam Tamzequil as 100% beneficial owner. A notarial deed (D-QX3UO, tier 2, Notarial Chamber of Calderra) records that he transferred 100% of the shares to Grasta Belpelo (born 1991-05-04), effective 2027-05-29. That date is after the register's last update. The Aurelia Business Register excerpt (D-HV8MG, tier 1, issued 2027-10-04, current under R3) also shows Grasta Belpelo as 100% holder since 2027-05-29. The customer's self-declaration (D-026CQ) names the same owner, so it matches the reliable evidence. This means the register is simply out of date. The current owner is confirmed by the notarial deed, a reliable source whose issuer is independent of the register's controlling authority. Our internal record (D-OSLYH) rates the customer standard risk with no alerts, so there are no grounds to suspect information is being concealed. All conditions for exception R2(b) are met, so the customer is asked to correct the register entry instead of the bank reporting the discrepancy.

The central register entry (D-J6PEQ, issued 2027-10-17, last updated 2027-04-01) lists Fentam Tamzequil (b. 1959-09-13) as the 100% beneficial owner. The Aurelia Business Register shareholder excerpt (D-HV8MG, issued 2027-10-04, so 15 days old and current under R3) is a tier 1 source. It shows Grasta Belpelo (b. 1991-05-04) as the 100% shareholder since 2027-05-29. These are different people, not a spelling or transliteration error, so there is a real discrepancy and exception (a) does not apply. The register looks out of date, but exception (b) also requires the other source to be independent of the register's controlling authority. Both registers are Aurelian government bodies, and no document says they answer to different authorities, so independence cannot be assumed. The customer's own declaration (D-026CQ) agrees with the business register, so no clarification is needed. The internal record (D-OSLYH) shows a standard risk rating and no alerts, so nothing calls for escalation. The default R2 action therefore applies: report the discrepancy to the central register within 14 calendar days.

Our internal risk record (D-OSLYH, 2027-10-10) rates the customer standard risk with no alerts, so there are no grounds to suspect concealment, and the higher-risk bar does not apply. The central register entry (D-J6PEQ, last updated 2027-04-01) still lists Fentam Tamzequil (born 1959-09-13) as the 100% beneficial owner. Two reliable sources show that Tamzequil gave up the shares on 2027-05-29, so the register is out of date. However, those two sources disagree about who the new owner is. The notarial deed (D-QX3UO, tier 2) names Wenvi Daloda (born 1991-05-04). The Aurelia Business Register excerpt (D-HV8MG, tier 1, issued 2027-10-04, current) names Grasta Belpelo, with the same birth date and the same start date of 2027-05-29. This is a completely different name, not a typing or transliteration error. The customer's self-declaration (D-026CQ, tier 3) matches the business register but not the deed. The internal record (D-OSLYH) shows a standard risk rating and no alerts. Because the reliable evidence contradicts itself about who the current beneficial owner is, the rules for correcting the register cannot be applied: rule (a) does not fit because this is not a typo, and rule (b) does not fit because the current owner is not reliably known. A report to the register could not state the correct owner either. Under R2 and R5, this contradiction, plus the declaration's mismatch with the deed, must go to a human officer rather than be resolved by guessing. I am escalating so that the officer can resolve who owns the company and file the required report to the register within the 14-day deadline.
